record.exact_prompt:
Create a publication-quality scientific mechanism illustration as a NEW PNG background. This is a new drawing, not a redraw. Choose an original coherent layout from the scientific mechanism below; the external reference images only explain related concepts and conventions. Do not copy reference typography, backgrounds, exact layout, colours, irrelevant objects, or any reference text.
The final image will have labels separately typeset in real fonts, so draw ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT: no letters, words, numbers, equations, plus/minus signs, pseudo-writing, legends or watermarks. Leave generous clean text-sized gaps beside each semantic object, in each module heading region, and beside arrows. Do not put an icon in a reserved text region. Necessary mathematical operators will be added later. Never make decorative title cards. There is no global title inside the image.
Visual language: quiet, elegant, flat two-dimensional academic diagram, pure white canvas, sparse outlined modules mixed with very pale solid colour regions. Use semantic colour grouping, a restrained consistent thin dark-grey arrow/outline system, simple flat shapes. At most one small flat outline icon per semantic module; equivalent modules share icon treatment. No repeated icon badges, no sticker/card dashboard aesthetic. Place any icon next to a blank heading line, not centred above it. Use only palette Blue #7B95C6, Cyan #49C2D9, Green #67A583, Sage #D0E2C0, Orange #F59C7C, Peach #FFC1A6, Rose #C85E62, with pale fills obtained by mixing a colour with white at 18–25 percent colour. Borders may use the stronger semantic colour. Normal paths dark #4C4D4F. Use colour locally, avoid continuous large saturated areas. All fills are uniform solid colour. No noise, grain, paper texture, bands, ripples, glows, halos, gradient shading, shadows, 3D extrusion, cubes or perspective.
Content and relation accuracy are more important than decoration. All arrows must have unambiguous sources and targets and exactly one arrowhead, only at the receiving end. Do not add speculative or redundant paths. Leave enough white space to add readable headings/variables with no overlap. Medium-wide approximately 3:2 or 16:10 canvas, generous margins. Details and layout autonomous; don't mimic a source diagram.

Scientific mechanism: two possible exogenous backgrounds, low and high, initially equally probable. Observing a factual event updates the background probabilities to one-quarter low and three-quarters high. This is abduction, not selection of a single background. An intervention then changes the response map, NOT the individual background. The same intervention map takes low background to outcome 2 and high to outcome 6. Pushing the posterior through this map gives a conditional counterfactual outcome distribution with masses one-quarter at 2 and three-quarters at 6, expected outcome5. Pushing the original equal prior through the SAME intervention map gives equal masses at2 and6, expected outcome4. Depict the update of a two-point background distribution and the same two response endpoints in a clear causal workflow; distinguish the conditional posterior path from the population prior path. A small factual evidence object connects to the update. Exactly two possible backgrounds and two outcome endpoints per distribution, no random-resampling/replacement of the person and no collapsed deterministic result. Corresponding low/high backgrounds and outcomes retain visual identities. Reserve labels for prior, observed fact, abduction, posterior, intervention response map, and outcome. Numeric masses and variables will be typeset later. The intervention module must represent changing a mapping; no syringe, pill, surgery, or misleading physical medical icon. Prefer a compact abstract mechanism rather than a generic infographic. Only the attached two diagrams are external mechanism references, not layouts to copy.
